To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the physicochemical characterization of the inclusion complexes of piperine with α- and β-cyclodextrins revealed the formation of GMs with molar ratios 1/2 and 1/1 and that the solubility and structure of the inclusion complexes were influenced by the cyclodextrin used.
the physicochemical and solubility properties of GMs of piperine with cyclodextrins were studied.
the solubility and dissolution behavior of the GM complexes are influenced by their molecular structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physicochemical characterization and the solubility behavior of the GM inclusion complexes of PP with αCD and γCD.
the physicochemical characteristics and solubility behavior of PP/CD inclusion complexes.
a novel approach to enhance the solubility and bioavailability of poorly water-soluble drugs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GM (PP/CD = PP/αCD) inclusion complex is the best candidate to improve the solubility and dissolution of piperine.
the solubility enhancement is due to the formation of a head-to-head type complex of PP with αCD, and the solubility decrease is due to the inclusion of PP with γCD.
the solubility enhancement of the inclusion complexes is mainly due to the formation of a complex structure, which is stabilized by hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the inclusion complex formation between piperine (a pungent ingredient) and cyclodextrins (CDs) is an effective way to enhance the solubility, which is important in the development of functional food products.
the inclusion complex of PP with αCD is superior to that of γCD in terms of solubility and dissolution rate.
the solubility and dissolution rate of GMs of PP with α- and β-CD are influenced by the inclusion complex structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GMs of PP/α- and γCD are promising candidates as a solubility enhancer for poorly soluble drugs.
it is possible to control the dissolution behavior of piperine by using the inclusion complex with cyclodextrin.
the inclusion complex formation of PP/α- and γ-CDs can enhance the solubility and dissolution behavior of the complex.
